problems.stem: An essay is due Friday 11:59 PM. Which split correctly uses a calendar versus a task list?
options: Both go on the calendar as all-day events
Calendar: a Thursday 6 to 8 PM 'draft essay' block; Task list: 'submit CAT100 essay' due Fri 11:59 PM
Both go in the task list with no date
Calendar: the 11:59 PM deadline only; nothing in the task list
problems.explanation: Fixed-time work (the draft block) belongs on the calendar; the deliverable with a due date and done state belongs in the task list.

problems.stem: Your task list shows 'read chapter 7', 'email advisor', and 'lab report' with no dates. Why do you keep missing things?
options: Tasks have no due dates, so nothing can surface or sort before it is late
The tasks should be calendar events instead
The list needs a different color theme
problems.explanation: Without due dates the system cannot tell you what is next. Adding a date to each task lets it sort and remind.

problems.stem: A project is due in 10 days and needs about 6 hours of work. You only scheduled the due date. What should you add?
options: Two or three work blocks across the 10 days that total about 6 hours before the due date
A second copy of the deadline
An all-day event on the due date
problems.explanation: The deadline is when it must be done. Scheduling work blocks ahead of it is how the 6 hours actually get spent.

problems.stem: Class starts at 10:00 AM and you need 15 minutes to walk there plus 5 minutes to open materials. When should the reminder fire?
options: At 9:40 AM, about 20 minutes before, matching travel plus prep
No reminder is needed for a recurring class
problems.explanation: Reminder lead time should cover what you must do first. A 'class now' alert gives no time to travel or prepare.
